utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, I would like the representatives of the office of the Prosecutor to introduce themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Geoffrey Nice is my name. INTERPRETER: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Geoffrey Nice is my name, Kenneth Scott sitting with me.

utterances.text: For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is an honour for me to introduce myself before this Court. My name is Mitko Naumovski and I am attorney for Dario Kordic not Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours, my name is Bozidar Kovacic and I am the Defence counsel for the accused Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Registrar, would you give me a piece of paper so I can be sure I'm spelling the names of the parties correctly. Thank you. Do not apologise for reintroducing yourself to the Tribunal, this is a frequent occurrence. Let me turn to the accused. They know why they are here. I would like to rapidly summarise the purpose of this meeting. First, excuse the Tribunal for the delay. We have been seized by an order of 30th September 1998 that was signed by McDonald who had been the confirming judge for the indictment against the accused, Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez. In respect of that order a new indictment was filed at the request of the Prosecutor. It has now been signed, it was signed on the 2nd of October; is that not right, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: And therefore, according to Rule 50B of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence, we must now have a further initial appearance of Mario Cerkez and Dario Kordic and that is what we're going to do. We will not go back to all of the formalities of Rule 62, but before the indictment is read I might first ask the Defence attorneys if this indictment has, in fact, been submitted to the accused and if they understood the contents of it before we read it? Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I can say as the Defence counsel for Dario Kordic, I can say that he has received the indictment in the that language he understands, that is the Serbo-Croatian language. He has studied it together with me and he does not understand, I think that is what he said, he does not understand what he is being indicted for.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The indictee Mario Cerkez has received the indictment. He has understood it in the language that he understands and he does understand what he is being indicted for and charged under the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Then, if Judge Rodrigues agrees with me, we can now read the indictment which will be done by Mr. Dubuisson, that is the reading of the indictment as confirmed by Judge McDonald on the 30th of September and signed by the office of the Prosecutor on October the 2nd. Mr. Dubuisson, if you would please do the following: When we come to the counts, for each count I will ask the accused to rise and to state whether they plead guilty or not guilty, which will avoid unnecessary waste of time which would force us to go back to the counts. Do you agree with that? I turn to the Defence attorneys.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Of course, we do agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Dubuisson, you can now read the indictment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: "The Prosecutor against Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez, amended indictment. The Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, pursuant to their authority under Article 18 of the Statute of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia. The Statute of the Tribunal charges: Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez with crimes against humanity, grave breaches of the Geneva Conventions and violations of the laws or customs of war. Background 1. The events alleged in this indictment took place against the background of the break-up of the former Yugoslavia. The Republic of Croatia declared its independence on 25 June 1991, the implementation of which was suspended until 8 October 1991. The Republic of Croatia was recognised by the European Community on 15 January 1992 and admitted by the United Nations as a member state on 22 May 1992. The Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina declared its independence on 3 March 1992 and was recognised by the European Community on 6 April 1992 and admitted by the United Nations as a member state on 22 May 1992. 2. At times relevant to the indictment, the Croatian Democratic Union (the "HDZ") was a principal and influential political party in Croatia. Some of the HDZ's stated goals were to establish "the sovereignty of the Croatian people" and their "inalienable right to self-determination, including the right to secession of the entire Croatian nation inside its historical and natural borders," and to promote "the economic and spiritual association between Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina which comprise (or constitute) a natural inseparable geopolitical entity and whose historical fate (or destiny) is directed toward partnership."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: If you would please indicate when they are quotes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 3. At times relevant to the indictment, the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina, (the "HDZ-BiH") was a principal Bosnia Croat political party in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Among the HDZ-BiH's stated goals were "securing the right of the Croatian people to self-determination, including the right to secession." 4. The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, (the "HZ H-B") proclaimed its existence on 18 November 1991, claiming to be a separate or distinct "political, cultural, economic and territorial whole," in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Among its purposes was the establishment of closer ties to or a union with Croatia, as evidenced by the HZ H-B's use of Croatian currency, the Croatian language and the granting of Croatian citizenship by Croatia to Bosnian Croats. The HZ H-B's presidency included a President, two Vice-Presidents and a Secretary. The President's powers included the appointment of executive and administrative authorities. On 28 August 1993 the HZ H-B declared itself the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, ("HR H-B"), with its two principal officers being a President and a single Vice-President. Neither the HZ H-B nor the HR H-B were ever recognised by the International Community, and the HZ H-B was declared illegal by the constitutional court of Bosnia and Herzegovina on or about 14 September 1992. 5. By Article 2 of the 18 November 1991 decision on the establishment of the HZ H-B, the HZ H-B (and later the HR H-B) consisted of the following municipalities in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina: Jajce, Kresevo, Busovaca, Vitez, Novi Travnik, Travnik, Kiseljak, Fojnica, Skender Vakuf (Dobretici), Kakanj, Vares, Kotor Varos, Tomislavgrad, Livno, Kupres, Bugojno, Gornji Vakuf, Prozor, Konjic, Jablanica, Posusje, Mostar, Siroki Brijeg, Grude, Ljubuski, Citluk, Capljina, Neum, Stolac and Trebinje (Ravno). By virtue of Article 4 of the same decision, the municipality of Zepce was added to the HZ H-B/HR H-B in about October 1992. 6. The Croatian Defence Council (the "HVO") the was established in or about April 1992 and was the HZ H-B's and HR H-B's supreme executive, administrative and defence authority. The creation of municipal HVOs was authorised and such HVOs were subsequently established beginning in or about June 1992 as the municipal executive and military power. The HVO and every HVO member were subject and accountable to the HZ H-B presidency, which in turn executed its powers and objectives through the HVO. 7. From approximately November 1991 to March 1994 various persons and groups associated or directed, instigated, supported or aided and abetted by the HDZ, the HDZ-BiH, the HZ H-B/HR H-B and HVO and various of their political, municipal and administrative bodies, armed forces, police, paramilitary and special units, caused, planned, prepared, instigated, supported, directed and engaged in a campaign of persecutions and ethnic cleansing and committed serious violations of international humanitarian law against the Bosnian Muslim population residing in the HZ H-B/HR H-B and the municipality of Zenica in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Accused and Superior Authority Dario Kordic 8. Dario Kordic, son of Pero, was born on 14 December 1960 in Sarajevo in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. He studied at the University of Sarajevo where he concentrated on political science and then worked as a journalist. 9. Dario Kordic was an active member of the HDZ-BiH and rose to positions of increasing power, authority and influence in the Bosnian Croat leadership. He was part of the highest circle of political and military leaders in the HDZ-BiH, the HZ H-B, the HR H-B and HVO. In 1991, Dario Kordic was named president of the HDZ-BiH in the municipality of Busovaca and also president of the Travnik Regional Community. As president of the Travnik Regional Community Dario Kordic co-chaired a meeting of the HDZ-BiH on 12 November 1991 where it was declared that "the Croatian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina finally has to start conducting a decisive and active policy which would bring about the realisation of our eternal dream a joint Croatian state." Several days later, on 18 November 1991, Dario Kordic was one of the leaders who signed the decision establishing the HZ H-B and became one of its two Vice-Presidents, in which position he continued until approximately August 1993. By virtue of his position as a Vice-President, Dario Kordic was also a member of the HZ H-B presidency, which also functioned as the HZ H-B's legislative body. When the HR H-B was declared in August 1993, Dario Kordic was named Vice-President, in which position he continued at times relevant to the indictment. Beginning on or about 10 July 1994, he became president of the HDZ-BiH. At times relevant to the indictment Dario Kordic represented himself and was regarded by others as a senior HVO official, and signed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Does it say -- there was an error in the French reading.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: He signed orders and documents as a senior HVO official. By his roles and positions, Dario Kordic exercised power, command and authority in and over the HVO and his activities and operations. 10. Dario Kordic, by virtue of his various offices, positions and authorities, his relationships with key Croatian and Bosnian Croat leadership figures and his political and military power in the HZ H-B/HR H-B, exerted power, influence and control over the political and military aims and operations of the HDZ-BiH, the HZ H-B, the HR H-B and HVO. Dario Kordic demonstrated power, influence, authority and control on numerous occasions and in numerous ways including, by example, making policy and strategic decisions, negotiating cease-fire agreements on behalf of the HVO, issuing orders that would directly or indirectly of a military nature or consequence, representing himself as a HVO Colonel, Vice-President or other senior HVO official, dressing in military attire, having a military operations room in his office at the PTT building in Busovaca, a countermanding cease-fire agreement when the terms were not suitable to him, appointing and dismissing persons to or from various offices, jobs and positions, issuing orders for the arrest or release of influential Muslims detained by the HVO, authorising travel and freedom of movement through various HVO-controlled territories, obtaining the release of stolen or seized vehicles or property, and negotiating the passage of relief convoys or United Nations vehicles through various checkpoints. Mario Cerkez 11. Mario Cerkez, son of Tugomir, was born on the 27th of March 1959 in the village of Rijeka, municipality of Vitez, in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. He worked as a car mechanic and a clerk at the SPS factory. 12. Mario Cerkez became the commander of the HVO Brigade in or about the municipality of Vitez (the "HVO Vitez Brigade") in 1992, and he remained in such position at all times relevant to the charges in this indictment. His position within the HVO meant that he was under the command of Tihomir Blaskic who was then the HVO Central Bosnia Operative Zone Commander. Mario Cerkez's authority and duties as a commander are set fort in the decree on the armed forces of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, dated the 17 of October 1992, which provides that a commander in his position was responsible for the combat readiness of the troops under his command and the mobilisation of the armed forces and police units and had the authority to appoint and dismiss commanders. 13. At all times relevant to the charges in this indictment Mario Cerkez, by virtue of the positions and authority described above, demonstrated or exercised his control in military matters in a variety of ways including, by example, negotiating cease-fire agreements with opposing civil and military figures from within the Muslim community, negotiating with United Nations officials, issuing orders to deploy troops and other units under the command and controlling the detention and treatment of detained civilians. General allegations 14. In each paragraph charging crimes against humanity, a crime recognised by Article 5 of the Statute of the Tribunal, the alleged acts or omissions were part of widespread, large-scale or systematic acts or conduct directed against Bosnian Muslim Civilian populations residing in the HZ H-B/HR H-B and the municipality of Zenica in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. 15. At all times relevant to this indictment, a state of international armed conflict and partial occupation existed on the territory of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. 16. All acts or omissions herein set fort as grave breaches of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, (hereafter "grave breaches"), recognised by Article 2 of the Statute of the Tribunal, occurred during such international conflict and partial occupation. 17. All the victims referred to in the charges contained in this indictment were at all relevant times persons protected by the Geneva Conventions of 1949. 18. The accused in this indictment were required to abide by the mandate of the laws and customs governing the conduct of war, including the Geneva Conventions of 1949. 19. Dario Kordic, from about November 1991 to approximately March 1994 is individually responsible for the crimes charged against him in this indictment pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Individual criminal responsibility includes committing, planning, instigating, initiating, ordering or aiding and abetting the planning, preparation or execution of any acts or omissions set fort in this indictment. 20. Dario Kordic, from November 1991 to approximately March 1994 is also alternatively criminally responsible as a superior for the acts of his subordinates pursuant to Article 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. A superior is criminally responsible for the acts of his subordinate if the superior knew or had reason to know that his subordinate was about to commit such acts or had done so and the superior failed to take necessary and reasonable measures to prevent further such acts or to punish his subordinate. As to each charge in the indictment, Dario Kordic, in addition to being individually responsible, knew or had reason to know, and it was foreseeable that persons subordinate to him were about to commit various crimes, persecutions and illegal acts, or had done so and failed to take necessary and reasonable measures to prevent such crimes, persecutions and acts or punish the perpetrators thereof. 21. Mario Cerkez, from about April 1992 to approximately August 1993 is individually responsible for the crimes charged against him in this indictment pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Individual criminal responsibility includes committing, planning, instigating, initiating, ordering or aiding and abetting the planning, preparation or execution of any acts or omissions set fort in this indictment. 22. Mario Cerkez, from about April 1992 to approximately August 1993 is also or alternatively criminally responsible as a superior for the acts of his subordinates pursuant to Article 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. A superior is criminally responsible for the acts of his subordinate if the superior knew or had reason to know that his subordinate was about to commit such acts or had done so and the superior failed to take necessary and reasonable measures to prevent further such acts or to punish the subordinate. As to each charge in the indictment, Mario Cerkez, in addition to being individually responsible, knew or had reason to know, and it was foreseeable that persons subordinate to him were about to commit various crimes, persecutions and illegal acts, or had done so and failed to take necessary and reasonable measures to prevent such crimes, persecutions and acts, or punish the perpetrators thereof. 23. The general allegations continued in paragraph 1 through 22, as well as the allegations in paragraphs 24 through 35 below, are re-alleged and incorporated in each charge. Charges 24. One of the principal aims of the HDZ-BiH, the HZ H-B, the HR H-B and the HVO was to control various municipalities and territories in Bosnia and Herzegovina and connect or unify them with the Republic of Croatia. To achieve this aim, the HDZ-BiH, the HZ H-B, the HR H-B and the HVO caused, planned, instigated, prepared and initiated, supported and executed a political military campaign to gain control of these territories and to ethnically cleanse them of, or substantially reduce and subjugate, the Bosnian Muslim population. This campaign was carried out by various practices, means and methods which demonstrated, by their pattern, consistency and frequency, that an orchestrated and widespread campaign was implemented throughout the HZ H-B/HR H-B and the municipality of Zenica from about the 18 of November 1991, when the HZ H-B proclaimed its existence to approximately the 1st of March 1994 when the Washington Agreement was signed. 25. In his various high ranking positions and through the power and influence that he exercised, Dario Kordic played a central role in developing, establishing and executing the policies, objectives and strategies of the HDZ-BiH, the HZ B-H, HR H-B and the HVO. Along with others, he launched, planned, instigated, prepared, ordered, committed and aided and abetted a political military campaign to persecute and terrorise Bosnian Muslims, which involved, or resulted in the commission of serious violations of international humanitarian law. Dario Kordic was a definite integral and important figure in the whole campaign and had power, authority and responsibility to direct, control and shape its policies and execution, and to prevent, limit or punish crimes violations or abuses which occurred or were carried out in the campaign. He publicly advocated the campaign's goals and encouraged and instigated the ethnic hatred, strife and distrust which served its ends. 26. Dario Kordic extended his fear of authority, commanded influence over a wide range of municipalities and was closely involved in preparing, instigating and carrying out the campaign's objectives and operations. Dario Kordic not only personally voiced and promoted the campaign's objectives and participated in various criminal acts, but was also aware of and had every reason to know in the highly charged and volatile environment of Bosnia and Herzegovina of the dangers, abuses and consequences of the campaign's policies and objectives and the courses of conduct that he and others set in motion. Persecution, oppression and violence against Bosnian Muslim civilians, institutions and property were fully foreseeable and no adequate steps were taken to prevent, stop or punish such abuses and violations. Dario Kordic knew or had reason to know that various subordinates and aiders and abettors were about to persecute and oppress Bosnian Muslims, or had done so, and failed to take the necessary and reasonable measures to prevent such acts or to punish the perpetrators. 27. As a HVO commander, Mario Cerkez implemented by military means the HDZ-BiH's, the HZ H-B's, the HR H-B's and the HVO's goals, practices and objectives, and committed and aided and abetted the persecution campaign. He was the commander of the HVO Vitez Brigade which was directly and actively involved in the wide-scale persecution against Bosnian Muslim civilians. Mario Cerkez also knew or had reason to know that various subordinates and aiders and abettors under his control were about to persecute and oppress Bosnian Muslim civilians or had done so and failed to take the necessary and reasonable measures to prevent such acts or to punish the perpetrators. 28. The campaign of persecution, violence and ethnic cleansing was perpetrated and carried out on a widespread or systematic basis by various means and methods, including attacks on cities, towns and villages with no military significance inhabited by Bosnian Muslim civilians and killing and causing serious injury to Bosnian Muslim civilians. Many of the attacks commenced early in the morning when most of the inhabitants were in their homes and asleep. At least 100 defenceless Bosnian Muslim civilians, including women, children, the elderly and the infirm were killed and many wounded or harmed in their homes or yards while attempting to hide or escape from the HVO attacks, or bombardments, or after they had been detained by the HVO. 29. Detention and imprisonment were other means used to persecute Bosnian Muslims who were systematically selected, detained and imprisoned in HZ H-B, HR H-B and HVO detention facilities on political, racial, ethnic or religious grounds. Imprisoned and otherwise detained Bosnian Muslim civilians were subjected to physical and psychological abuse, including beatings and sexual assaults and suffered inhumane deprivations of basic necessities, such as adequate food, water, shelter and clothing. There was often little or no medical attention and overcrowded and unsanitary conditions. 30. As part of the persecutions, Bosnian Muslims were forced to proclaim their allegiance to the HZ H-B, HR H-B, and/or the HVO, or face losing their jobs. Many Bosnian Muslims, were dismissed or removed from government, municipal and other positions or relegated to positions of no real power or authority. 31. Many of the Bosnian Muslims who were imprisoned and detained were also forced to dig trenches in hostile and otherwise hazardous conditions, were used in forced labour, used as hostages to promote the HZ H-B/HR H-B and HVO political military objectives and also used as human shields. Some such persons were killed in the course of being detained and forced to engage in such activities. 32. The persecution again Bosnian Muslims was also accomplished by encouraging instigating and fomenting hatred, distrust and division on political, racial, ethnic or religious grounds by propaganda speeches and otherwise. 33. The widespread persecution of Bosnian Muslims also included coercing, intimidating, terrorising and forcibly transferring such civilians from their homes and villages. Many of the persecuted Bosnian Muslims were either killed, transferred or forced to move to Muslim-dominated areas outside the municipalities of Vitez, Novi Travnik and Busovaca. Many of the detained or transferred civilians were taken to HVO checkpoints, and then made to walk to Bosnian Muslim territory. 34. To promote and advance this ethnic cleansing, various members of the HDZ-BiH, the HZ H-B, the HR H-B and the HVO, together with their agents and others instigated, caused and engaged in the wanton and extensive destruction and plundering of Bosnian and Muslim property with no military justification. Bosnian Muslim dwellings and buildings, as well as civilian personal property and livestock were destroyed or severely damaged. Bosnian Muslim businesses were blown up and destroyed. Many of these acts and much of this damage was meant to ensure that the Muslim inhabitants could not or would not return to their homes and communities. In addition, many Bosnian Muslim buildings, sites and institutions dedicated to religion or education were targeted for destruction or otherwise damaged or violated. 35. As a result of the persecution and ethnic cleansing campaign, the Bosnian Muslim civilian population was substantially reduced and relocated from those areas of the HZ H-B/HR H-B where the HDZ-BiH, the HZ H-B, HR H-B and the HVO and their leaders and agents seized control. COUNT 1 Persecutions 36. From about November 1991 to approximately March 1994, Dario Kordic, together with various members of the HDZ-BiH, the HZ H-B/HR H-B, and the HVO and their leaders, armed forces and agents caused, planned, instigated ordered or committed or aided and abetted the planning, preparation or execution of a crime against humanity. That is, the widespread or systematic persecutions of Bosnian Muslim civilians on political, racial, ethnic or religious grounds, throughout the HZ H-B/HR H-B and the municipality of Zenica in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. 37. This campaign of widespread or systematic persecutions was perpetrated, executed and carried out by or through the following means: (A) attacking cities, towns and villages inhabited by Bosnian Muslim civilians. (B) killing and causing serious junior or harm to Bosnian Muslim civilians, including women, children, the elderly and infirm, both during and after such attacks. (C) encouraging instigating and promoting hatred, distrust and strife on political, racial, ethnic or religious grounds by propaganda, speeches and otherwise. (D) selecting detaining and imprisoning Bosnian Muslims on political racial ethnic or religious grounds. (E) dismissing and removing Bosnian Muslims from government, municipal and other positions. (F) coercing intimidating, terrorising and forcibly transferring Bosnian Muslim civilians from their homes and villages. (G) physical and psychological abuse inhumane acts, inhuman treatment, forced labour and depravation of basic human necessities, such as adequate food, water, shelter and clothing, against Bosnian Muslims who were detained or imprisoned. (H) using detained or imprisoned Bosnian Muslims to dig trenches. (I) using detained or imprisoned Bosnian Muslims as hostages and human shields. (J) wanton and ex-extensive destruction or plundering of Bosnian Muslim civilian dwellings, buildings, businesses and civilian personal property and livestock; and (K) the destruction and wilful damage of institutions dedicated to Muslim religion or education.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kordic, would you rise, please. What has just been read, that is paragraphs, 36 and 37, constitute count 1, the charge of persecution, the registrar will read the exact wording of the count and then I will ask you what you intend to plead.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: By these acts and omissions Dario Kordic committed: Count 1: A crime against humanity as recognised by Article 5(h), 7(1) and 7(3) (persecutions on political racial or religious grounds) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kordic, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED KORDIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, I have understood this count of the indictment and I believe that I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You are not guilty. You are saying that. But are you going to plead not guilty? You must -- the terms must be very exact, that is to tell your counsel that you are pleading not guilty, that the, all the proceedings will be developed further to your plea of not guilty. All right, Mr. Naumovski do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I know in Serbo-Croat there is a distinction in the language made. I'm sure that you are saying that you are not guilty, but according to this procedure you must say whether you plead guilty or not guilty, plead guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED KORDIC
utterances.text: I shall repeat once again, Your Honours, I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated, Mr. Kordic, because we are going to move to Mr. Cerkez and we will come back to you for further counts. Please be seated and, registrar, please continue count 2, persecutions, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: From about 1 April 1992 to September 1993, Mario Cerkez, together with various members of the HDZ-BiH, the HZ H-B/HR H-B and the HVO and their leaders, armed forces and agents caused, planned, instigated ordered or committed or aided and abetted the planning, preparation or execution of a crime against humanity, that is, the widespread or systematic persecutions of Bosnian Muslim civilians on political racial, ethnic or religious grounds in the municipalities of Vitez, Busovaca, and Novi Travnik in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. 39. This campaign of widespread or systematic persecutions was perpetrated, executed and carried out by or through the following means: (A) attacking cities towns and villages inhabited by Bosnian Muslim civilians. (B) killing and causing serious injury or harm to Bosnian Muslim civilians, including women, children, the elderly and infirm, both during and after such attacks. (C) encouraging, instigating and promoting hatred, distrust and strife on political, racial, ethnic or religious grounds by propaganda, speeches and otherwise. (D) selecting, detaining and imprisoning Bosnian Muslims on political, racial, ethnic or religious grounds. (E) coercing, intimidating, terrorising and forcibly transferring Bosnian Muslim civilians from their homes and villages. (F) physical and psychological abuse, inhumane acts, inhumane treatment, forced labour and depravation of basic human necessities, such as adequate food, water, shelter and clothing against Bosnian Muslims who were detained or imprisoned. (G) using detained or imprisoned Bosnian Muslims to dig trenches. (H) using detained or imprisoned Bosnian Muslims as hostages and human shields. (I) wanton and extensive destruction and/or plundering of Bosnian Muslim civilian dwellings, buildings businesses or civilian personal property and livestock; and. (K) the destruction and wilful damage of institutions dedicated to Muslim religion or education.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Cerkez, would you rise, please. You heard the paragraphs referred to count 2, which involve you specifically. As I did for your co-accused, I'm going to ask you whether you plead guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise, but I think we have a small technical problem here. Point 38, which was read out, refers, first of all, to the time from the 1st of April 1992 until September 1993. In the order of the Court allowing the amended indictment, the Prosecutor made an oral amendment and this was stated in the Court's order of the 30th of September in the penultimate paragraph, and on this page it says until September 1993, or rather they were substituted with the words until about August 1993. At any rate, in point 38, it should be until about the 31st of August 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think that the Prosecutor is going to provide an explanation. It seems there was an order from Judge McDonald which was rendered on 30 September, which authorised the substitution in paragraph 38. Is that correct, Mr. Prosecutor, to change September 1993 from around August? Perhaps you were not informed. Let me give the floor to Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, there was an application to amend, to extend the date to September 1993, and that application was granted. I'm a little -- I have another concern about paragraph 39 that I haven't yet resolved, but maybe you would rather deal with paragraph 38 to begin with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let's deal with things in the proper order. Mr. Kovacic, are you satisfied? You may be seated Mr. Nice. Please be seated. Mr. Kovacic, are you satisfied with the Prosecutor's answer? Myself, I had received a notice of an order rendered by Judge McDonald, but I didn't mention it before, but I did know about it, where she had granted the Prosecutor's request for authorisation to modify the amendment and to allow the substitution in paragraph 38 of the draft and amended the indictment of the expression around August 30, around the 31st of August by September 1993, were you not informed of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is quite clear to me now. So, the important thing is that the order and indictment give the same dates, regardless of the word "about".

From about the first of January 1993 to approximately the 31st of March 1994, Dario Kordic, together with members of the HZ H-B/HR H-B and the HVO and their leaders, armed forces and agents caused, planned, instigated, ordered or committed or aided abetted the planning, preparation or execution of the imprisonment, unlawful confinement and inhuman treatment of Bosnian Muslims at the following at about the following locations in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina: Kaonik Prison, Vitez Cinema Complex, Vitez Veterinary Station, SDK Offices in Vitez, The chess club in Vitez, Dubravica Elementary School, Municipal Building in Kiseljak, Kiseljak Barracks, Rotilj village, Nova Trgovina and Silos. 45. From about the 1st of January 1993 to approximately the 31st of January 1994, Dario Kordic, together with members of the HZ H-B/HR H-B and the HVO and their leaders armed forces and agents caused planned instigated ordered or committed order aided and abetted the planning preparation and execution of, the use of Bosnian Muslim detainees to dig trenches in hostile, hazardous and combat conditions in the municipalities of Kiseljak, Vitez, Busovaca, Novi Travnik and Zepce, which resulted in a number of such detainees being killed or injured. 47. utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well, this initial appearance has now been conducted. This is an initial appearance further to rule 62 but we're not going to set the date for the trial, we are still involved in Status Conferences. Yes, I will, of course, give you the floor, but let me finish first. I thought that perhaps we could set a date for a subsequent Status Conference, but that would also give you the opportunity to speak as well as the accused and the Prosecutor. I simply wanted to adjourn to another date for a Status Conference in front of myself because now it is a bit late to set up such type of conference, but I would like to have your opinion on that. First we turn to the Defence. Let me give you the floor, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't want to take up much time, perhaps we can redact the transcript later. However, as regards one point, though, the transcript when paragraph 19 of the indictment was read out, in transcript, this is 10.00, 26 minutes, 4 seconds, it is supposed to say Dario Kordic and the transcript mistakenly says Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kovacic. Let me remind you that the conditions under which the transcripts are prepared are complicated, but I can a sure you, I'm speaking subject to anything the registrar wants to tell me, but first the transcripts are reread after this hearing by the transcribers who are doing extremely difficult work, as are the interpreters, they spend several hours after the hearings comparing what they have transcribed which is done on the spot with the tapes, so that they can, first of all, prepare an initial version of the transcript. I think it is then sent to all parties for any comments they wish to make and to the judges.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. It is sent to all the parties and to the judges so, if necessary, any corrections may be made. I think it is only after that that the transcript is put on the internet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Therefore, you have all guarantees and to the contrary both today and as soon as you have your first draft transcript, may I suggest that you make any comments you like. This is very important. We have this problem constantly at hearings and it is very important for the parties to make comments, because after that the transcript becomes a legal document. Have you any further comments you would like to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. No thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Naumovski, do you have any comments you would like to make?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I have no objections with regard to what we have done so far, but I would like to take advantage of this opportunity to ask you for one thing. First of all, this initial appearance is being held when we planned to have the Status Conference continued, and I just wanted to ask, if possible, that we determine when the Status Conference will be continued, the one we started previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We're going to try to set a date, because I think there is no point beginning today, there are many things that are involved in this case. I am not forgetting it, nor is the pre-trial Judge, but there are many things that have to be done in a pre-trial conference. Let me remind you that this hearing will start further obligations on the part of the Prosecutor. Let me turn to Mr. Nice who will provide a whole series of documents, unless he has already done so. They have certain matters which we have to settle. I was waiting for the initial appearance, including the request for a separate trial for Mr. Cerkez, which we will respond, of course. I would like first to turn to the Prosecutor and ask whether there is any comments or any other documents to provide further to the amended indictment which is going to call out another 30 days for any other preliminary motions that might be filed, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There are no other documents to be served today. We are anxious that the next Status Conference should be as early as convenient to the Chamber. There are a number of matters, as Your Honour correctly says to be dealt with, principal among them, is, of course, serving on the Defence the material upon which the amended indictment has been confirmed. We have 30 days to do that, and we are anxious to do that as quickly as possible, but we can't do that task until questions of witness protection are finally resolved; therefore, there some is pressure to have an early hearing date in everyone's interest and in the interest of getting the trial on as soon as may be. The other matters that are outstanding in relation to production of documents under Rule 68 and other matters, are all in hand. The Court will remember that there are also some outstanding motions which were held in abeyance right from the beginning of this year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That any Status Conference would be likely to consume some time, if it's to be heard through to a conclusion of all outstanding matters, probably a hole day, at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I'm not sure that myself as the pre-trial Judge can do that all in one day. Mr. Fourmy, do you think the 28th in the morning, would that be a proper date?

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: Mr. President, in order to try to meet as soon as possible, perhaps the 28th would be a good date. I think the Prosecutor is available on that date, I don't know whether the Defence is. Are there other Defence counsel? If you allow me to remind you, ordinarily for Mr. Kordic there are two other counsels who excused themselves for today knowing that Mr. Naumovski would be present, but we have to check with them as to their schedules for the 28th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Might they come from the United States on the 28th in the morning and then set the hearing for 9.00 or perhaps 9.30 for the interpreters, and for the detention service? What time could we begin, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, we could begin at 9.30 without any problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That's not quite what I was asking. I was going to suggest 9.00. Would 9.00 be possible? Maybe that's more complicated.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: If it is an exceptional case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, all right, I understood. All right, if it's not exceptional, we can't, but if it's exceptional, we can. All right, let's try, because on Wednesday we have the Blaskic hearings at 2.00 in the afternoon, we have to think about the interpreters work. Let's put 9.00 -- all right, 9.30, we'll say 9.30 to 12.30, would that be enough for a break if it is the same interpreter team? Would that be enough?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, there won't be any problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Naumovski, could you inform Mr. Geneson and Mr. Turner that this Status conference will be on the 28th at 9.30 in the morning and to be available for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Absolutely, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. We're not going to take up the many, many problems that we have in this case. We have a very, very busy schedule. I would not like to conclude this Status Conference without having first given the floor to the accused and ask them what they feel about their current detention conditions. Mr. Kordic, how are your detention conditions at this moment? You may rise, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED KORDIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I thank you for your kindness in asking me the question. We are very pleased that after the meeting held by the President of the Court, Mrs. McDonald and Mrs. Sampayo were held with all the detainees, a letter was received from Ms. McDonald telling us that there will be improve according to some of the points we asked for and we expect this to implemented by the new year. We have been transferred to an older section of the Netherlands prison and we are moving today and I hope that going back to the old building that the conditions have been furnished which were much better than where we were for the moment, but we persevered and we're going back. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CERKEZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just hope that when we return that the conditions will be much better than they were in the past 14 days where we were lodged. Because the rooms were really bad and the conditions were poor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What your co-accused said, you might say that there would be improvements, work is in progress. Where do things stand as regards that work?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As you said, this is a work in progress and we're doing the best we can to allow the detainees to go back to their cells.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Just a bit more patience and then everything will fall into place. All right, this initial appearance, I think we have to resume another trial in about 15 minutes, I would like to adjourn this hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 11.52 a.m. to be reconvened on the 28th day of October, 1998 at 9.30 a.m.
